news.title: Australia World Cup star Cristian Volpato reportedly tests positive for cocaine after being stopped twice
news.lede: Australia international Cristian Volpato has reportedly tested positive for cocaine after being stopped twice by police for speeding in Sydney on the same night, just days after representing the Socceroos at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Football News: Australia's Cristian Volpato, fresh off his World Cup appearances, reportedly tests positive for cocaine after being stopped by police for speeding. The young midfielder's career takes a concerning turn as authorities investigate.

news.title: Didier Deschamps’ France legacy explained: How he rebuilt FIFA World Cup-winning Les Bleus into a football powerhouse
news.lede: Dynasties rarely end with a bang. More often, they fade quietly, leaving only numbers and memories to tell the story. Didier Deschamps departs the France dugout after 187 matches in charge, having won 122 of them, drawn 32 and lost only 33 — a remarkable 65.2% win rate. But statistics alone cannot explain his tenure.

news.title: Argentina behaviour after World Cup final was ‘intolerable’, says De la Fuente
news.lede: Spain head coach hits out at ‘acts of aggression’. Fifa investigation into incident yet to result in sanctions. Spain’s head coach, Luis de la Fuente, has hit out at the “intolerable, unacceptable” behaviour of Argentina players in the immediate aftermath of Sunday’s World Cup final. At the forefront were Nahuel Molina and Leandro Paredes, who attacked Rodri and Eric García respectively at New York New Jersey Stadium as Spain’s players celebrated winning the World Cup for a second time in the country’s history.

news.title: Guardiola snubs Italy! Manager chooses personal break over rebuilding Azzurri after World Cup failures
news.lede: Pep Guardiola has formally turned down the opportunity to become Italy's next national team manager despite the Italian Football Federation (FIGC) making him its leading candidate to rebuild the Azzurri after another disappointing FIFA World Cup campaign. Football News: Pep Guardiola has turned down the opportunity to manage Italy's national football team, choosing to prioritize a personal break over rebuilding the Azzurri after their World Cup failures. Reports reveal the Italian Football Federation's efforts to persuade him, but Guardiola remains committed to his decision for time away from football.

news.lede: Chattanooga leaders believe the city’s welcoming hospitality played a role in the Spanish national team’s World Cup win. Soon, La Roja will add another star to their logo to symbolize their second FIFA World Cup win. Spanish soccer will forever leave a mark on the Scenic City. news.title: Lionel Messi quietly made Vozinha's family's World Cup dream come true before final
news.lede: Lionel Messi reportedly ensured that four members of Cabo Verde goalkeeper Vozinha's family could attend the 2026 FIFA World Cup final after arranging tickets for them at his own expense. The gesture took place before Argentina's title clash against Spain at the New York New Jersey Stadium, where Messi's side suffered a 1-0 defeat after extra time. The story only emerged after the final, with Messi having made no public mention of his involvement. Argentine journalist Yanina Latorre revealed that Messi purchased a large number of tickets during the tournament for people who could not afford to attend matches.

news.title: Aston Villa reject Serie A club’s ‘tiny offer’ for World Cup finalist
news.lede: Aston Villa have turned down Juventus’ ‘tiny offer’ for Emiliano Martinez, per journalist Gianluca Di Marzio. The Serie A club are looking to sign a new goalkeeper to compete with Michele Di Gregorio for the starting role. They submitted a bid worth around £5 million for Martinez, which was quickly rebuffed. Villa are under no immediate pressure to sell, as the Argentinian is under contract until 2029.
